summary: Congressional involvement in D.C. governance spans multiple domains this week, from a judge's assertion that Congress controls Kennedy Center naming decisions to Senator Slotkin's renewed commitment to statehood as a priority. Coverage also reflects on the anniversary of the National Guard deployment to Washington, D.C., with advocates emphasizing how the incident underscores the need for local autonomy. Without statehood, Congress can override D.C. laws, control District property and institutions, and deploy military forces within the city's borders without local consent.
